issues.text: After hang detection, the code guards process.kill() with isinstance(process, multiprocessing.Process), but since the flusher uses a spawn context, the actual object is a SpawnProcess which does not inherit from multiprocessing.Process, so the isinstance check is always False in production and the old hung process is never killed; a new process is created for the same shard anyway, and both processes will concurrently non-destructively flush the same shard, producing duplicate segments to the buffered-segments topic. This is independent of the --flusher-processes flag value.
issues.zh: hang 偵測後舊 flusher process 不會被 kill，卻已補上新 process，兩者會同時 flush 同一組 shard

issues.text: spans.buffer.max-flush-segments effectively changes meaning from a global per-flush cap to a per-process cap: since each SpansBuffer now only sees 1/N of the shards, flush_segments' ceil(max_flush_segments / len(assigned_shards)) formula results in an aggregate cap across N processes of roughly N × max_flush_segments instead of the original single value.
issues.zh: spans.buffer.max-flush-segments 從全域上限變成每 process 上限

issues.text: SpanFlusher's class-level default behavior changed: previously max_processes unset meant one process total; now `max_processes or len(buffer.assigned_shards)` means unset defaults to one process per shard — the highest-resource-usage option — while the CLI default is still pinned to 1, so the two defaults point in opposite directions and any new caller that doesn't set max_processes explicitly could unknowingly spawn many processes.
issues.zh: SpanFlusher 的類別預設從「一個 process」變成「每個 shard 一個 process」

issues.text: _create_process_for_shard (singular) is dead code with no callers anywhere in the repo, and its name misleadingly suggests a "restart just one shard" capability that doesn't actually exist (it would restart the whole process, interrupting other shards on it too).
issues.zh: _create_process_for_shard（單數）是沒有呼叫端的死碼，且它的名字暗示了一個不存在的能力

issues.text: test_basic's newly added time.sleep(0.1) doesn't actually wait, because time.sleep was already monkeypatched to a no-op earlier in the same test, so the comment claiming it gives flusher threads time to process is misleading and the test's flakiness protection has no effect.
issues.zh: test_basic 新增的 time.sleep(0.1) 不會產生任何等待，因為 time.sleep 在同一個測試開頭已被換成 no-op

issues.text: test_flusher_processes_limit only asserts bookkeeping fields (process counts, shard-to-process map size) that are trivially true from the constructor logic, but never asserts that the produced `messages` list actually contains all expected segments — so the real risk of this change, whether shards split across multiple processes still get fully flushed without loss or duplication, is completely uncovered, and the heavily-modified _ensure_processes_alive has no test touching it at all (which is why F-001 isn't caught by tests).
issues.zh: test_flusher_processes_limit 只驗證帳面數字，沒有驗證「兩個 process 共用四個 shard 仍然不漏資料」

issues.text: The new shard_tag used in metrics has unbounded cardinality: it's a comma-joined string of the shards a process owns, which changes on every Kafka rebalance and combination of --flusher-processes, so metrics like spans.buffer.segment_size_bytes (fired per segment) can produce an unbounded number of distinct tag values.
issues.zh: 新增的 shard metrics tag 是不受控的 cardinality

issues.text: The same shard-list value is tagged inconsistently across nearby metrics calls — some use the tag key `shard`, others use `shards` for the identical value — forcing dashboard/query authors to remember two different tag names for the same thing.
issues.zh: 同一段程式的 tag key 也不一致：flusher.py:185 與 192-196 用 shard，flusher.py:199 用 shards，兩者的值卻是同一個 shard 清單

issues.text: spans.buffer.flusher_unhealthy is now incremented once per shard owned by an unhealthy process instead of once per unhealthy-process event, inflating the counter by a factor of shard-count and breaking the semantics existing dashboards/alerts assume.
issues.zh: flusher_unhealthy 的計數語意被放大：把 spans.buffer.flusher_unhealthy 改成對該 process 底下每個 shard 各 incr 一次

issues.text: The class docstring's new claim "Creates one process per shard for parallel processing" only holds when max_processes is None; the actually deployed process-spans consumer uses the CLI default of 1 (one process for all shards), so the docstring describes the opposite of the real default deployment behavior.
issues.zh: class docstring 新增的敘述與實際預設行為相反

issues.text: The newly added max_processes constructor parameter is missing from the class's :param documentation block.
issues.zh: 新增參數未進 :param 區塊

issues.text: join()'s outer deadline check does a `break` out of the loop entirely instead of `continue`, so once the deadline is hit, every remaining process in the list is skipped and never gets terminate() called on it — changing behavior from "always terminate after waiting" to "stop terminating anything once one process times out".
issues.zh: join() 在 deadline 到期時 break，會讓其餘 process 連 terminate() 都被跳過

issues.text: The `if not process: continue` guard at the start of _ensure_processes_alive can never be true, since self.processes only ever holds SpawnProcess or threading.Thread objects (neither defines __bool__/__len__) and is never populated with None.
issues.zh: _ensure_processes_alive 開頭的 if not process: continue 永遠不會成立

issues.text: SpanFlusher's constructor requires a full SpansBuffer argument but only ever reads its assigned_shards attribute before discarding it and building N new SpansBuffer instances internally, meaning the signature demands more than the class actually needs and the passed-in buffer creates an extra unused Redis connection in the parent process.
issues.zh: SpanFlusher 只從傳入的 buffer 取 assigned_shards 卻要求傳整個 buffer

issues.text: The new --flusher-processes CLI flag has no lower-bound validation: passing 0 falls back (due to Python falsy-0 behavior in `max_processes or len(...)`) to "one process per shard", the opposite of what a user passing 0 likely intends and the highest resource usage option; passing a negative value crashes with an opaque KeyError instead of a clear parameter error.
issues.zh: --flusher-processes 對 0 與負值沒有防護：0 的效果與使用者意圖相反，負值以 KeyError 收場

issues.text: The diff adds a hasattr/isinstance Python convention example to CLAUDE.md that is unrelated to the span buffer multiprocess change, making it harder to trace via git log why/when that convention was added if bundled into this PR.
issues.zh: CLAUDE.md 新增的 hasattr / isinstance 段落與本次 span buffer 變更無關

issues.text: The CLAUDE.md edit leaves an extra blank line before the code fence that wasn't there prior to this change.

submit()'s Redis memory check now queries the entire cluster-wide INFO once per SpansBuffer (i.e. once per flusher process) instead of once total, redundantly repeating the same cluster-wide query N times per submit call (though the resulting used/available ratio itself remains correct, and this code path is skipped entirely at the default max-memory-percentage=1.0).
issues.zh: submit() 的記憶體檢查對每個 buffer 各查一次整個 Redis cluster 的 INFO

open_questions.text: After scaling --flusher-processes to N, Kafka producer and Redis connection counts roughly multiply by N; does the target cluster have headroom for that, and what value of N is actually planned?
open_questions.zh: 把 --flusher-processes 調到 N 之後，Kafka producer 與 Redis 的連線數會變成約 N 倍；目標叢集有這個餘裕嗎？打算把 N 設到多少？

open_questions.text: Are the two modified tests in test_consumer.py stable in CI, given they now depend on real threads and Redis and one of them has a no-op'd time.sleep turning the flusher thread into a busy loop?
open_questions.zh: tests/sentry/spans/consumers/process/test_consumer.py 的兩個測試在 CI 上是否穩定？
